Agent Ready

Built to be read by machines

Flavor DS is delivered to agents, not just to people. Every fact on the site has a machine-readable twin, and a memory layer decides what an agent needs for the task in front of it — while the global rules stay in force no matter what the task is.

What is machine-readable

Everything below is generated from one source at build time and served as a static file or an MCP tool. Nothing is a hand-written summary that can drift.

  • MCP tools

    13 tools over Streamable HTTP (https://flavor-ds.vercel.app/api/mcp) or stdio — memory, contract, tokens, contrast pairs, components, icons, native, Figma, Canvas feedback.

  • /agent/index.json

    The memory index: 87 chunks, each with id · kind · priority · tags · summary · source path · text. What flavor_recall ranks.

  • /agent/rules.md

    The twelve global rules, each tied to the guard that enforces it. Priority 0 — always returned, never ranked.

  • /llms.txt · /llms-full.txt

    The llms.txt convention: a short orientation for crawlers and a full dump of every chunk for agents without MCP.

  • DTCG tokens

    tokens.json in the W3C Design Tokens format, plus flavor.css, contrast.json (17,280 computed pairings, +0.05 margin) and meta.json (axes + defaults).

  • Native exports

    FlavorTokens.swift (typechecked against the SwiftUI SDK) and .kt, generated from the same source. platform.css maps HIG / M3 chrome.

  • Behaviour contracts

    behaviors.js: keyboard/focus contracts as data-fds-* attributes — 40 asserted key sequences, shared by HTML and React.

  • Guards

    Every rule has a check in npm test; an agent verifies rather than assumes. flavor_canvas_feedback closes the loop with human review.

The global rules

Priority 0. Returned first on every recall — empty task, id fetch, 500-token budget — and each one names the guard that enforces it. An agent cannot get a task-specific answer without them.

  1. Semantic tokens only. Components, templates and product code reference `--surface-*`, `--text-*`, `--border-*`, `--accent-*`, `--success|warning|danger|info-*`, `--space-N`, `--radius-control|field|container|media|round`, `--font-*`, `--duration-N`, `--ease-*`. Never a primitive
  2. Contrast is computed, never asserted. Every text/background pairing in the semantic tier already clears WCAG AA
  3. Theme is nine attributes on `<html>`, nothing else: `data-hue data-sat data-mode data-contrast data-bg data-radius data-density data-font dir`. Set them; do not fork stylesheets. Defaults: hue=brand sat=regular mode=light contrast=aa bg=primary radius=rounded density=regular font=expressive dir=ltr.
  4. Radius follows the axis. `--radius-control`
  5. Logical properties only
  6. Icons come from the sprite. `<svg class="fds-icon" data-icon><use href="/icons/sprite.svg#hi-NAME-outline"></use></svg>`
  7. Motion on tokens. `transition-property` names exact properties
  8. Targets have a floor. Interactive elements are ≥ 40×40
  9. Behaviour comes with the component. Menu, Tabs, Dialog, Listbox and Tooltip get their keyboard/focus contracts from `behaviors.js`
  10. Rule of three before promoting anything into the shared system; one-offs stay product-local. Deprecations alias for one minor and are removed in the next major.
  11. Media background: `--surface-page` is transparent; text placed directly on the photo binds `text-on-media`; text in opaque panes keeps `text-primary`.
  12. Verify, don't assume. After generating UI, run the guards

Full text with guard references: /agent/rules.md. Source: scripts/build-agent-index.mjs.

How indexing and retrieval work

Six steps, deterministic end to end. No embeddings, no model in the loop — the same task always produces the same recall, so the ranking is testable and the test runs in CI.

  1. 1

    Build

    scripts/build-agent-index.mjs runs inside npm run build:tokens. It reads the same sources the site and the MCP read — meta.json, figma.json, TOKENS.md, GOVERNANCE.md, componentDocs.ts, productNav.ts, behaviors.js, the native spec — and emits the index. There is no hand-maintained copy: if a component is added to the docs, it is in the index on the next build; if it is removed, it is gone.

  2. 2

    Chunk + tag

    Each unit of knowledge becomes one chunk with a stable id (component-button, tokens-space, template-projects…), a kind (rules, contract, tokens, component, template), a one-line summary, and tags: the words in its title/summary plus a small curated alias list — the words people type that a doc summary doesn't contain ("modal" for dialog, "kanban, gantt, asana" for the project template).

  3. 3

    Prioritise

    Every chunk carries a priority. 0 = the global rules — always returned. 1 = the contract nothing works without (theme axes, setup, token tiers, guards, MCP call order). 2 = tokens and components — returned when the task matches. 3 = worked examples and process (templates, governance, canvas). Priority damps the score (÷ 1 + p × 0.25) so a specific match in a reference chunk still surfaces, but on a tie the contract wins.

  4. 4

    Recall

    flavor_recall({task}) — same code as the demo below (packages/mcp/src/recall.mjs). The task is split into terms, lightly stemmed, and expanded through a synonym map at 0.4 weight so an expansion never outranks the literal word. score = Σ tag hit ×3 + title ×2 + summary ×1 + text ×0.5, then damped by priority. Tasks that look like they build UI ("build", "screen", "form", "page"…) always also get axes + setup.

  5. 5

    Budget

    The payload has a token budget (default ≈6k, 4 chars/token). Rules always fit. Ranked chunks are added in score order until the budget is spent. Every chunk that was ranked but not loaded is listed under omitted with its id and one-line summary — the agent sees what it is missing and fetches it explicitly with {ids}. Nothing is silently dropped.

  6. 6

    Apply, then verify

    The agent builds against the returned chunks — semantic tokens only, the contract's nine attributes, the component's markup — then runs npm test. The guards falsify the work: lint:tokens, wcag-qa, check-templates, check-polish, test-behaviors, adoption. For reviewed work, flavor_canvas_feedback returns the human review as selector-scoped, token-named tweaks. Recall itself is tested: scripts/test-recall.mjs asserts rules-always, ranking on representative tasks, the budget, and determinism.

The agent's call order

1. flavor_recall({ task })          → rules (always) + contract (if building UI) + ranked chunks, budgeted
2. flavor_recall({ ids: [...] })    → anything listed under "omitted" that you actually need
3. flavor_get_component(id) · flavor_find_icon(q) · flavor_get_theme(axes) · flavor_get_contrast_pairs(hue)
4. build — semantic tokens only, nine <html> attributes, component markup as documented
5. npm test                         → the guards falsify the work
6. flavor_canvas_feedback           → apply the human review, by selector and token

Root CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md in the repo say the same thing in two lines, so an agent that opens the folder without MCP still lands on rules.md and the index.
